small_guidance:
- The conv_transpose3d is dominating runtime (~10.2ms vs 5.3ms baseline). Tuning the softmax/sigmoid block sizes won't close the gap since the conv is untouched. At minimum, ensure x.contiguous() is avoided when already contiguous, and consider channels_last_3d layout for the conv output to make the softmax-over-C reduction contiguous.
- In the existing fused kernel, BLOCK_C=64 (next pow2 of 64) with BLOCK_S=128, num_warps=8 should be the sweet spot; drop the BLOCK_S=32 config since the spatial dim (16·64·64=65536) is large and small tiles waste launch overhead.
- The sigmoid(softmax(x)) formulation can be simplified: since softmax outputs are in (0,1), `sig = 1/(1+exp(-sm))` is a few flops on register data — already fused, fine as-is.
large_guidance:
- Replace nn.ConvTranspose3d with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile) computing the input×weight outer product and scatter-adding into the output grid with stride=2/padding=1/output_padding=1 index math. This is the heavy op (FLOPs ~ N·IC·OC·KD·KH·KW·D_in·H_in·W_in) and where all the headroom lives.
- Alternatively, implement as a gather-based GEMM: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), where each output position iterates over the (kd,kh,kw) positions whose strided/padded input index lands on it (the "gather form" of conv-transpose). Use a tiled GEMM with BLOCK_M=32, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=16 and autotune; this avoids atomic adds entirely.
- Fuse the bias add, softmax-over-C, and sigmoid into the conv-transpose epilogue so the OC=64 output is reduced in-register before store. With OC=64 fitting in a single tile, a persistent kernel keyed on (N, output-spatial) can compute the full OC vector, do the softmax max/sum reduction, apply sigmoid, and store — avoiding a second kernel launch and the full read/write of the 16·64·16·32·32 intermediate.
